title: POC SLO acceptance playbook — TTFT vs TPOT, sampling & schedule
topics: TTFT vs TPOT definition and use cases
p95/p99 target setting and representative workloads
timeline and stakeholders for POC acceptance
summary: AE+SE aligned with CedarPoint on hybrid SLOs: TTFT for interactive UI latency, TPOT for batch/throughput endpoints. Agreed on p95 and p99 guardrails differing by endpoint; sampling and shadow traffic plan to run 2 week baseline then stress sweep. Next: Redwood to deliver SLO matrix and measurement playbook; CedarPoint to provide traffic samples and a prioritized prompt set.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-06-14 15:00 UTC // Duration: ~52m // Recorders: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Lena (CedarPoint Head of ML), Trevor (Platform), Amira (CTO)

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call — and then we'll jump into the SLO playbook.
[00:20] Amira (CedarPoint): Hi — yes here. Thanks. We're particularly focused on two services: the user-facing chat and a backend summarization batch job.
[00:30] Marcus (Redwood): Great, that maps cleanly to TTFT and TPOT discussions. I want to set expectations: TTFT (time-to-first-token) is what your end users will feel in chat; TPOT (total per‑token) is more about cost and throughput for batch.
[01:05] Lena (CedarPoint): Quick question — our product team cares more about p95 than p99 for chat, but security/regulatory wants p99 for SLA. How do you recommend reconciling?
[01:22] Marcus (Redwood): Common. We usually propose a two-tier SLO: p95 target for product experience and a p99 SLA for enterprise guarantee. For the POC acceptance we'll set internal goals and an external gating SLA.
[02:00] Trevor (CedarPoint): Can you give concrete numbers? We run Llama-3-ish models, avg prompt 220 tokens, response 140 tokens. Currently hitting median 170ms for first token in our beta, but that was on single GPU and not production.
[02:27] Sofia (Redwood): Helpful. For similar profiles we typically propose TTFT p95 <= 350ms and TTFT p99 <= 700ms as starting points for hosted low-latency configs. TPOT targets depend on throughput and cost — we suggest per-token 98th percentile cost guardrails rather than latency.
[02:55] Lena (CedarPoint): That p99 700ms seems high — our product team wants sub-500 p99 ideally. Is that realistic?
[03:07] Marcus (Redwood): Possibly if you go dedicated and optimize batching, KV cache warming, and quantization. There's always a tradeoff: lower latency at higher infra cost. We'll show modeling during the POC.
[03:30] Amira (CedarPoint): On security — we need VPC + KMS + audit logs. Does Redwood's private deployment impact latency samples?
[03:42] Sofia (Redwood): Private deployments add a small network delta, 10–50ms typical depending on customer network egress. We'll include a network baseline in measurement. Also we'll run a shadowing test within your VPC to measure realistic TTFT.
[04:10] Trevor (CedarPoint): Great. For measurement, what tooling does Redwood use? We want reproducible artifacts for our compliance team.
[04:20] Marcus (Redwood): We use an internal benchmark runner that emits request-level telemetry: TTFT, total tokens, queue time, and model variant. We'll provide a measurement playbook — scripts + Grafana dashboards + raw CSVs for the POC.
[05:05] Sofia (Redwood): Ok let's talk acceptance criteria. Proposal:
 - Chat interactive (TTFT): p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 600ms for canary on dedicated pool.
 - Chat fallback/cheap variant: p95 <= 450ms, p99 <= 900ms as a degraded acceptance.
 - Batch summarization (TPOT): median throughput >= 1200 tokens/s per node, p95 token-latency target less critical but must not exceed N seconds per job — we'll model.
[05:50] Lena (CedarPoint): Those are helpful start points. We need to pilot both heavy (long prompts) and light (short prompts) traffic. Can Redwood help synthesize traffic?
[06:05] Marcus (Redwood): Yes, we'll take a month of your traffic logs and distill a sampling distribution. For the POC we'll run: 1) 48h baseline with production traffic replay (1:1 shadow), 2) 72h stress sweep varying batch sizes and seq lengths, 3) 1 week steady-state sampling to validate run rate.
[06:40] Amira (CedarPoint): Shadowing concerns — will user data leave our VPC?
[06:46] Sofia (Redwood): No, shadowing is internal within your VPC or private deployment. We only receive anonymized telemetry and the raw logs if you permit; otherwise we work with anonymized traces.
[07:05] Trevor (CedarPoint): For the stress sweep, how do you control for cache warm vs cold? Last time our KV cache warmed super fast and skewed TTFT.
[07:20] Marcus (Redwood): Good catch. Our plan includes cold-start runs and warm runs. We'll document cache hit-rate and include TTLs in the runbook. Cold-starts will be isolated and reported separately.
[07:40] Lena (CedarPoint): Are you able to measure sequence-length-conditioned SLOs? e.g., p95 for <=256 tokens vs for >512 tokens?
[07:50] Marcus (Redwood): Absolutely. We'll stratify metrics by prompt+response length buckets. That's part of the SLO matrix.
[08:20] Sofia (Redwood): On thresholds, one thing customers miss: TTFT for streaming APIs can be impacted by model sampling parameters (top-p, temperature) because token-generation time varies. We'll capture generation time variability in the measurement.
[08:42] Trevor (CedarPoint): Okay. For acceptance gating — do we require both TTFT and TPOT to be within target simultaneously, or can one be traded for the other?
[08:58] Marcus (Redwood): For the POC we recommend gate per route: interactive route must meet TTFT thresholds, batch route must meet TPOT throughput targets. If chat route fails but batch passes that's ok for partial acceptance; final go/no-go should be a decision with your product and infra leads.
[09:30] Amira (CedarPoint): Timeline question — we want a POC in four weeks. Feasible?
[09:35] Sofia (Redwood): Tight but doable if we get your traffic samples and priority prompt set within 3 business days. Our typical timeline: week 0: setup + traffic ingestion, week 1: baseline replay, week 2: stress sweeps & tuning, week 3: iterate and finalize SLO matrix, week 4: acceptance report.
[10:05] Lena (CedarPoint): We'll prioritize chat + one batch pipeline. We'll send data extracts and a prioritized prompt list.
[10:15] Trevor (CedarPoint): One more — what about model fallbacks? If primary fails we want automatic routing to a cheaper model; do you measure mixed-model SLOs?
[10:27] Marcus (Redwood): Yes, Redwood's smart routing can fall back to a quantized or smaller variant. For SLOs we'll run mixed-model simulations and include a degradation curve: how TTFT changes when routing percentage shifts.
[11:00] Sofia (Redwood): Let's capture explicit acceptance matrix items:
  - Route name
  - Primary model and fallback model(s)
  - Traffic sample size and buckets
  - TTFT p95/p99 targets per bucket
  - TPOT throughput/efficiency targets
  - Measurement method (shadow/replay/stress)

[11:45] Lena (CedarPoint): Sounds good. On measurement outputs, compliance will want raw CSV + an executive summary.
[11:55] Sofia (Redwood): We'll provide both — CSV exports, Grafana permalinks, and a one-page executive summary with callouts for regressions.
[12:20] Trevor (CedarPoint): Any recommended runbook for sampling frequency? We have diurnal traffic and a huge evening spike.
[12:30] Marcus (Redwood): Recommended: include at least two weekday peaks and two weekend runs; also a long-tailed 24h sample and a focused 3h peak-stress run. That gives you coverage of steady-state and extremal behavior.
[13:05] Amira (CedarPoint): Risk question — what are the top 3 risks that could block acceptance?
[13:12] Sofia (Redwood): 1) Network variance in your VPC causing inflated TTFTs, 2) Unrepresentative traffic samples skewing metrics, 3) Model mismatch (your infra using a different model family). We'll map mitigations in the playbook.
[13:45] Lena (CedarPoint): Anything we need to provision? GPUs, quotas?
[13:50] Marcus (Redwood): For a dedicated pilot we recommend reserving 2 nodes (A100 or equivalent) for the 72h stress sweep to get stable measurements. If you can't, we can run on hosted capacity but results may vary.
[14:10] Sofia (Redwood): Okay, let's do a quick recap and next steps.

[14:20] Sofia (Redwood): Recap: Redwood will draft SLO matrix, measurement playbook, and sampling schedule; CedarPoint provides traffic logs + prompt set and confirms GPU availability. We'll aim to start the baseline within 7 days.
[14:40] Amira (CedarPoint): Good. Can you include a cost estimate for the dedicated test nodes in that doc?
[14:46] Sofia (Redwood): Yes, cost delta for dedicated vs hosted for the POC and projected per-token cost estimates.
[15:00] Trevor (CedarPoint): Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[15:05] Sofia (Redwood): Thanks, we'll send the docs. Meeting end.
